why_section.heading: Three things GPT Image 2 does better

items.title: Pixel-Perfect Text Rendering
items.body: Posters, thumbnails, and infographics get readable headlines and labels in one shot. No more Photoshop overlays or garbled text.

items.title: Cross-Image Consistency
items.body: The same character, product, or style holds across multiple panels. Build storyboards, product series, and IP characters that stay on model.

items.title: Image-to-Image That Preserves Identity
items.body: Upload a reference photo and the model keeps the face, product SKU, or pose intact. Great for headshots, restoration, and on-model shots.

items.q: How is GPT Image 2 different from Midjourney or Stable Diffusion?
items.a: GPT Image 2 has three clear advantages: (1) pixel-level text rendering — readable poster titles and infographic labels in one generation, (2) cross-image consistency — same character or product across multiple frames, (3) strong image-to-image identity preservation. Use Midjourney for pure aesthetic / illustration; use GPT Image 2 when text, identity, or product accuracy matters.

items.q: Can I use these prompts commercially?
items.a: Yes — generated images are typically usable for commercial purposes (review your Studio plan terms for specifics). The prompt templates themselves are derived from community sources and curated. We replace any specific celebrity or brand names with placeholders so your output is unique to you.

items.q: What is the {argument} syntax I see in some prompts?
items.a: Some prompts include placeholders like {argument name="product name" default="laptop"}. In the Workbench, these become editable input fields — change the value and the prompt updates automatically. This lets one template cover dozens of variations.

items.q: Are these prompts free to use?
items.a: All prompt templates are free to copy and adapt. Generation requires Studio credits — new users get a free trial allowance. 1K resolution costs 6 credits per generation, 2K costs 10 credits.

items.q: What's the difference between text-to-image and image-to-image prompts?
items.a: Text-to-image prompts (poster, infographic, food shot) generate from scratch using the description. Image-to-image prompts (action figure, sticker, photo restore, cinematic portrait) need you to upload a reference photo — the model preserves the identity while applying the new style.

items.q: Why are some prompts in JSON format and others in plain text?
items.a: Complex compositions (infographics, posters, thumbnails, product shots) use a structured JSON format that gives the model clearer instructions for layout, text positioning, and components. Simpler prompts use natural language. Both formats work — pick whichever feels more natural for your edits.
